Thanks for the demo last week — Novum is excited about the performance numbers. Our legal team attached redlines to the MSA and the Order Form (see Novum_MSA_redlines_v3.docx). There are three live points where we need clarity before procurement will proceed:

Can your team confirm Redwood's approach to each of these? We're aiming to land terms this week. If easier, happy to hop on a quick call with contracts.

  * 3) offer an explicit customer opt-in flow on the Order Form for training access?

Monica — reviewed Novum's redlines and their three asks. High-level thoughts below and a proposed compromise paragraph (see also attached RFC language).

1) Output ownership: we can agree that outputs delivered to Novum as part of the service are licensed to Novum for their internal use and productization, with a retained non-exclusive right for Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified derivatives for improving our services. Crucial to preserve: our right to use aggregate telemetry and model improvements that are not traceable to Novum data.

Proposed language (short):
"Customer owns output generated by the Service that is specifically and solely produced from Customer-provided input. Subject to Customer's written opt-out in the Order Form, Redwood retains a limited, non-exclusive right to use de-identified, aggregated output or derived signals for the purpose of service quality, safety, and model improvement, provided such use cannot be traced back to Customer or Customer Data."

2) Training/data use: we should accept an opt-in model on Exhibit A: default = no training/retention beyond ephemeral request-level logs required for troubleshooting; training/retraining on customer data only with explicit checkbox opt-in in the Order Form and documented scope. This meets their ask while allowing an opt-in commercial upsell.

3) Feedback license: we should narrow telemetry to metrics (latency, error rates, anonymized usage counters) and exclude sample-level retention/labeling unless customer opts in.

Attachment: Draft_Clause_Retention_and_Training.txt (proposed wording + fallback options).

Sean/Ben — product-runbook checks: will the opt-in flow require any architectural changes (e.g., separate storage paths, KMS scopes)? If so, outline cost/time. Laura — I'll incorporate this into a single cover paragraph to send to Novum along with a tracked change MSA.

Jake — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. Appreciate the urgency; see below a single-package compromise we can accept and ship to procurement if it meets Novum's needs. If this is OK we'll follow up with a tracked-change MSA and an updated Order Form (Exhibit A) and provide a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Summary of what Redwood proposes:
- Output ownership: Novum will own outputs generated from Novum inputs. Redwood reserves a limited, non-exclusive right to use aggregated and de-identified derivatives for service quality, safety, and model improvement that cannot be re-associated to Novum.
- Training/data use: default behavior in the MSA/Order Form will be no training or model retention beyond ephemeral logs for troubleshooting. Training on Novum data will require an explicit opt-in on Exhibit A that specifies scope, duration, and compensation.
- Feedback license/telemetry: Redwood will limit telemetry collected to operational metrics by default (latency, error rates, anonymized counters). Any sample-level retention or use for supervised labeling will require customer opt-in.

Action items:
1) Novum: confirm you accept the proposed paragraph below and we will issue a tracked-change MSA + updated Exhibit A (adds opt-in checkbox + scope fields).
2) Redwood legal (Laura): finalize tracked language and prepare a single-pass MSA redline.
3) Product (Sean): confirm technical gating for opt-in storage separation and estimated ETA/cost.

Proposed short paragraph we would put in the MSA/Exhibit A:
"Customer retains ownership of Outputs generated from Customer-provided Input. Unless Customer expressly opts-in on the Order Form for Training Use, Redwood will not use Customer Data or Outputs to train or improve models. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified derivatives and operational telemetry that cannot be re-associated with Customer Data for the limited purposes of service quality, safety, and model improvement. Any Customer opt-in for Training Use will be set forth in the Order Form, including the scope, duration, and any applicable fees."

If Novum confirms by COB Monday (25-May-2026) we will prepare the DocuSign and loop procurement to close.

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Contracts
Redwood Inference
